## Quick Fix
- **Branch:** `chore/library-real-data` (tip `6adc86a`, your last commit)
- **Status:** CHECK_RED

### Problem
`pnpm check` fails on `src/routes/library/page.spec.ts:96`:
```
ERROR "Conversion of type 'undefined' to type 'string' may be a mistake..."
ERROR "Tuple type '[]' of length '0' has no element at index '0'."
```

Root cause: `vi.fn(async () => ...)` infers a zero-arg call signature, so `fetchMock.mock.calls` is typed `[][]` (tuple of zero-length tuples). `c[0]` then errors because the empty tuple has no element at index 0; `as string` cast becomes unsound TS.

Vitest itself passes the test (vitest doesn't enforce TS call-arg narrowing the way `svelte-check`/`svelte-kit sync` does), but `pnpm check` is part of our merge/deploy gate.

### One-line fix

In `src/routes/library/page.spec.ts:90`, give `vi.fn()` a typed call signature so `mock.calls` carries the `[string]` arg tuple:

```ts
const fetchMock = vi.fn<(url: string) => Promise<{ ok: boolean; json: () => Promise<{ entities: never[] }> }>>(
    async () => ({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ entities: [] }) }),
);
```

Then line 96 stays as: `const urls = fetchMock.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);` (no `as string` cast needed — c[0] is already `string`).

Alternative if Vitest's generic typing makes that awkward: `const urls = fetchMock.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0] as unknown as string);` — the double-cast escape hatch. Cleaner but uglier.

Pick the first form unless Vitest's generic ergonomics push back. Either way, satisfy `pnpm check`.

### Verification
- `pnpm check` → 0 errors
- `pnpm test src/routes/library/page.spec.ts` → still 6/6 pass (semantics unchanged)
- `pnpm test` → 503/503

- `git add src/routes/library/page.spec.ts`
- Subject: `test(#chore-67): fix typed mock signature in #71 regression guard`
